title: Mara and the Weather
premise: Felix Vasquez, night librarian in a city that never quite sleeps, has spent fifteen years guarding a family secret: the woman everyone called her mother was really her aunt, and her real mother, Mara, vanished the night of a fire no one will discuss. When a stranger named Ivo appears at the aunt's funeral calling the family by the name nobody uses, Felix discovers he holds the old photographs—and the truth about what Mara did, and what was done to her. As the house sale deadline looms, Felix must choose between the loyalty that kept her silent and the justice Mara never received, finally forgiving the stranger in the photographs: herself, the child who survived by forgetting. She signs the sale only after placing Mara's name back into the family record.
about_author: Emrys Fairweather is the pen name of a former night-shift archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed photographs in a coastal city library. Their fiction explores how families curate memory the way libraries curate silence.

chapters.title: The Hour of Almost
chapters.summary: Felix, on her night shift, practices the art of almost saying things—cataloguing a patron's lost book she secretly knows the location of. POV: Felix. Beat: establish her lifelong habit of protective silence and the loneliness beneath it.

chapters.title: Funeral Weather
chapters.summary: At her aunt Rosa's funeral, rain that won't commit to falling. A stranger, Ivo, offers condolences using the surname 'Maren'—a name nobody has spoken in fifteen years. POV: Felix. Beat: the crack in the wall of forgetting.

chapters.title: What the House Keeps
chapters.summary: Felix returns to the family house to prepare it for sale and finds Rosa's locked study untouched. She catalogs rooms like library shelves, avoiding one. POV: Felix. Beat: dread dressed as tidiness.

chapters.title: The Man Who Used the Name
chapters.summary: Ivo waits outside the library. He claims Rosa wrote to him for years and that he has photographs Felix has never seen—Mara, alive, smiling, dated after the fire. POV: Felix. Beat: vertigo; her foundational memory wobbles.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Almost
chapters.summary: Flashback woven through a sleepless day: the fire, the aunt who took her in, the story she was given—Mara abandoned her. POV: Felix. Beat: sympathy for the lie, understanding why she accepted it.

chapters.title: Photographs of a Living Woman
chapters.summary: Ivo shows her the photographs. Mara in another city, another decade, holding a child who isn't Felix. POV: Felix. Beat: jealousy and relief tangled—Mara built a life without her.

chapters.title: Rosa's Ledger
chapters.summary: Felix breaks into the locked study and finds Rosa's ledger: payments, dates, and a recurring entry labeled only 'M.' The last entry is three weeks before the funeral. POV: Felix. Beat: the lie had an accountant.

chapters.title: The Librarian's Rule
chapters.summary: A quiet interlude at work; Felix helps a young patron find a book about a fire, and realizes she has never once searched her own family's records. POV: Felix. Beat: the professional instinct to preserve truth turns inward.

chapters.title: Ivo's Version
chapters.summary: Ivo tells his story: he was Mara's friend, then Rosa's correspondent, paid to keep Mara's location from Felix until Rosa died. POV: Ivo. Beat: the stranger becomes human; loyalty as its own kind of cage.

chapters.title: The Buyer
chapters.summary: The house sale accelerates—a developer's lawyer pushes for a fast close. Felix signs nothing yet, stalling. POV: Felix. Beat: external pressure becomes the clock the whole story runs on.

chapters.title: What the Fire Report Says
chapters.summary: Felix pulls the archived fire report: the fire was ruled arson, and the sole suspect was never named—only initials. M.V. POV: Felix. Beat: the ground shifts; Mara may have been accused, not guilty.

chapters.title: Rosa's Last Letter
chapters.summary: In the ledger's lining, a letter Rosa never sent: an admission that Rosa testified falsely, trading silence for custody of Felix. POV: Felix. Beat: the mother-figure becomes the betrayer; grief without a grave.

chapters.title: The Name Nobody Uses
chapters.summary: Felix researches 'Maren' and finds it was Mara's chosen name after she fled the accusation—her mother spent fifteen years being no one so Felix could be someone. POV: Felix. Beat: loyalty and truth revealed as the same wound.

chapters.title: Ivo's Confession
chapters.summary: Ivo admits he kept the photographs back for years, paid by Rosa, because he believed hiding the truth protected Felix—and because he loved Mara and feared what she'd done. POV: Ivo. Beat: forgiveness becomes possible only after anger.

chapters.title: The Developer's Deadline
chapters.summary: The sale closes in ten days; the lawyer threatens to void everything if Felix delays again. She must decide what the house is worth. POV: Felix. Beat: the clock tightens; money versus memory.

chapters.title: Finding Mara
chapters.summary: Using the photographs and Ivo, Felix traces Mara to a coastal town two hours away—and learns Mara died two years ago, never knowing Rosa had confessed. POV: Felix. Beat: justice arrives too late for its subject.

chapters.title: The House of Almost
chapters.summary: Felix walks the house one final time and finds, behind the study shelving, the box Mara left the night of the fire: everything she couldn't carry, left for the daughter she thought would come looking. POV: Felix. Beat: the house itself was the letter.

chapters.title: What Mara Left
chapters.summary: The box: Mara's own account of the fire—she saw who set it, Rosa's business partner, and fled rather than testify against a man the town loved. POV: Felix/Mara's letters. Beat: the climax of truth; the accused was the witness.

chapters.title: The Record
chapters.summary: Felix brings the evidence to a journalist and a retired archivist, refusing the police, who closed the case long ago. Justice outside the law: the record is corrected where records live. POV: Felix. Beat: agency; she stops almost saying it.

chapters.title: Closing
chapters.summary: The sale closes. Felix signs, but first removes one item: the photograph of Mara at nineteen, which she keeps. The house becomes someone else's; the name comes with her. POV: Felix. Beat: letting go of the container, keeping the contents.

chapters.title: Mara and the Weather
chapters.summary: Felix visits Mara's grave in the coastal town, tells her the truth out loud, and forgives her—for leaving, for being no one, for being believed guilty. The rain finally falls properly. POV: Felix. Beat: grief completes; the title lands.

chapters.title: The Night Shift, After
chapters.summary: Months later, Felix shelves a donated box of family photographs for the archive, catalogued fully, nothing almost about it. A patron asks her name; she gives all of it. POV: Felix. Beat: quiet resolution—she becomes a person who says things.
